checks: Verified source 30917746e40e143c §4 (2)–(4), §5 and §1 for the tied profile. The draft keeps the obstruction on the same prescribed menu and actual fixed body, without claiming all minimizing menus or a variationally minimizing body.

The cited singleton theorem makes all selected normalized own directions approach the three canonical orientations as an orbit. After relabeling, the margins converge uniformly on each edge. The opposite-vertex cap has strictly negative constant limiting edge margin, and the other two limiting margins have single transverse zeros at t=1/3 and t=2/3. Thus disagreement from the ordinary profile is confined to shrinking neighborhoods of those points, inside [1/4,3/4] for small parameters. This works for every minimizing orbit choice.

For any finite nonnegative convex restriction F on an edge, the Jensen bound on the interval centered at t of length one half gives F(t)≤2∫₀¹F on [1/4,3/4]. The disagreement set therefore contributes at most 2η times the full F-integral. The middle-third average of F is at most one third of its total integral by integrating the stated midpoint inequality. Since the limiting cap profile is 1/3 plus one third on that middle third, its field-weighted integral is at most 4/9 of the full integral.

On each outer fiber exactly one ramp is fully saturated at one, with the other two at zero. For each fixed edge normal and physical position x the three outer points have barycenter the middle point. Convexity therefore gives I₀≤R/3 after integration; no equality of field values at different bases is assumed. Hence I₀/(I₀+R)≤1/4 and the resulting bound is 13/36+η/2. The deficit at η=0 is exactly 1/12, giving the strict threshold η<1/6.

With the constant field the own per-edge limit is exactly 4/9, each outer per-edge average is 1/3, and all four fibers have identical perimeter. Its limiting efficiency is 13/36. Together with the uniform upper bound this proves the limit of the supremum. The normalized depth is (V+q)/(4V), with the same limit by q/V→4/9.

For the actual tied profile all real product fibers are K, the sampled family is compatible, and the total mass is 4V. The tied-profile theorem gives continuity, nonnegativity and strict own-interior concavity. Strict concavity around g gives positive f(g), and continuity gives positivity near g. The own chart theorem gives differentiability there. Under an affine barycentric symmetry, positive affine denominators correspond bijectively, and area is preserved, so the energy and tied profile are invariant. These check the actual smooth theorem hypotheses without importing a local-body-minimum assumption.

dependencies.mapping: Use the same body, profile and positive width and buffer, its actual unique middle maximizer, saturated matched outer fibers, cyclic own profile, and localization to the three ordinary orientations. The stated q limit gives the normalized smooth depth limit.

Use the complete lattice base with four identical positive triangle fibers, d=2, and their actual canonical hull B×K. The normalized tied profile is independent of the base and has the required continuity and strict concavity; its covariance norm is the single-fiber covariance norm.

Use its own-interior differentiability identity ∇_y log f(Y)=a_Y at every point in a positive interior neighborhood of g, in the same body-tied setting. No cross-fiber touching or marked-homothety equality is needed.

overlap.comparison: Uses exactly the same convex physical-field cone and an exact efficiency obstruction for ordinary closed caps on a different 31-site triangle product. The present four-site example treats the positive-width capture ramp and an actual smoothed singleton menu, with limit 13/36.

Its tied common separator is conditional on a local minimum over actual bodies and includes an augmented boundary response. This fixed-body example assumes no body extremum and tests only the prescribed averaged smooth cap profile. Neither assertion implies the other.
Provides the actual tied profile and its concavity, but treats buffered hard caps and does not calculate the smooth menu efficiency.

readability: Here the boundary profile averages the actual Ψ cap capture values, including the saturated outer values. It does not average the strip derivatives used for the menu coareas. The efficiency supremum is over fields for each parameter pair, and the upper bound is uniform over that cone.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: For this prescribed actual smooth menu, the entire nonnegative normal-dependent convex field cone has efficiency at most 13/36+η_(ε,h)/2<4/9 for sufficiently small parameters. Both its supremum and the normalized smooth depth tend to 13/36, including for the tied energy profile.
